candidates.evidence: Only weak partial resemblance: a strong low-frequency band near 98 cm-1 and a weak band near 282 cm-1 are compatible with some reported SnS Raman patterns. However, SnS literature bands expected near 160, 190 and 218 cm-1 are absent (residual at those positions is consistent with noise). Literature values were not checked against a reference in this sandbox, so this is a guess, not a match.

Layered Ga-chalcogenide family, but I could not confirm a ~98 cm-1 dominant mode for GaTe from a reference. Weak features checked near 134-140 cm-1 are not significant (amplitude about 1.4 sigma). Not a supported identification.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given (material_hint is null), so there is nothing to test. The spectrum is not identified with confidence. The two significant bands at 98.5 and 281.6 cm-1 do not match any reference I could verify offline, so the candidate ranking is low-confidence only.

limits: Identification is not possible from this data. The spectrum has only two significant features (98.5 and 281.6 cm-1) on a sloped background, over 60-1090 cm-1 with about 0.96 cm-1 sampling.
No reference library or literature was consulted; the sandbox is offline. Candidate materials are low-confidence guesses, and no literature provenance is claimed.
Excluded by absence of significant bands: GaSe-type bands near 134, 213 and 308 cm-1 (fitted amplitudes not significant at 213 or 308 cm-1; 134 cm-1 is about 1.4 sigma).

The 98.5 cm-1 band is fit with a single symmetric Voigt (FWHM 7.8 cm-1, gamma = sigma). An unresolved doublet cannot be excluded at this signal-to-noise; the residual is white, so a single band is adequate at this level.
The 281.6 cm-1 band has amplitude 2527 +/- 648 (about 4 sigma) and FWHM 1.9 +/- 0.7 cm-1. It is real but weak, and its width is poorly constrained.
No cosmic-ray spikes: the largest residual is 3.0 sigma, so no single-point outliers were found. No Si substrate line at 520.7 cm-1.
Polarization and layer number cannot be determined from one unpolarized spectrum with no angle series. Temperature (295 K) and 532 nm excitation were used only as context.

The folder name was not used as evidence. To identify the material, the full spectrum (0-60 and 1090+ cm-1), a reference spectrum or library, and ideally angle-resolved or multi-laser data are needed.
